goal.hinglish: Setup, Python, math, data aur databases — woh base jis par poora AI engineering khada hai.
goal.en: Setup, Python, math, data and databases: the base every AI system stands on.

intro.hinglish: AI engineering ka pehla din code likhna nahi, environment banana hai: ek virtual environment, git, secrets ke liye `.env`, aur Docker ka basic idea. Reproducible setup har job aur take-home me check hota hai, aur leak hui API key sabse common rejection reason hai.
intro.en: Day one of AI engineering is not writing code, it is building an environment: a virtual environment, git, a `.env` for secrets, and the basic Docker idea. Reproducible setup is checked in almost every job and take-home, and a leaked API key is a common rejection reason.

real_life.hinglish: Jaise ghar ki chaabi bahar mat chhodo, waise API key code me mat likho. `.env` local rehti hai, `.gitignore` usse git se bahar rakhta hai, aur `.env.example` team ko sirf naam batata hai.
real_life.en: You do not leave your house key outside, and you do not hard-code an API key. `.env` stays local, `.gitignore` keeps it out of git, and `.env.example` tells the team only the key names.

takeaway.hinglish: Agar naya laptop clone karke README follow karte hi sab chal jaye, setup sahi hai.
takeaway.en: If a fresh clone plus the README just works, the setup is right.

note.hinglish: Comment lines skip hoti hain, aur secret wali key mask ho jati hai.
note.en: Comment lines are skipped and the secret-looking key is masked.

prompt.hinglish: `parse_env(text)` likho jo comment/blank lines skip kare, `KEY=VALUE` ko split kare, aur jis key me `KEY`, `TOKEN` ya `SECRET` ho uski value `***` kar de. Phir diye gaye text par chala kar `env` print karo.
prompt.en: Write `parse_env(text)` that skips comments and blank lines, splits `KEY=VALUE`, and replaces the value with `***` when the key contains `KEY`, `TOKEN` or `SECRET`. Run it on the given text and print `env`.

exercises.starter:
def parse_env(text):
    env = {}
    # loop over lines, skip comments, split once on '='
    return env

env = parse_env('''
# local only
API_KEY=sk-live-123
MODEL="gpt-4.1-mini"
LOG_LEVEL=info
''')
print(sorted(env))
exercises.solution:
def parse_env(text):
    env = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith('#'):
            continue
        key, _, value = line.partition('=')
        key = key.strip()
        value = value.strip().strip('"')
        if 'KEY' in key or 'TOKEN' in key or 'SECRET' in key:
            value = '***'
        env[key] = value
    return env

env = parse_env('''
# local only
API_KEY=sk-live-123
MODEL="gpt-4.1-mini"
LOG_LEVEL=info
''')
print(sorted(env))

hint.hinglish: `line.partition('=')` pehle `=` par todta hai, isliye value me `=` ho to bhi safe hai.
hint.en: `line.partition('=')` splits on the first `=`, so a value may contain more.

intro.hinglish: AI engineer pehle software engineer hota hai. Type hints, dataclasses, validation, async calls, retries aur tests hi daily LLM code ko reliable banate hain. Model badal jayega, ye habits nahi.
intro.en: An AI engineer is a software engineer first. Type hints, dataclasses, validation, async calls, retries and tests are what make daily LLM code reliable. Models change; these habits do not.

real_life.hinglish: Restaurant order ki parchi ki tarah: model, tokens aur price likhe hon to bill galat nahi hota. Bina structure ke har call ek alag dictionary hoti hai.
real_life.en: Like a restaurant bill: when model, tokens and price are written down, the total is not wrong. Without structure every call is a different dictionary.

takeaway.hinglish: Boundary par validate karo, andar typed objects use karo.
takeaway.en: Validate at the boundary, use typed objects inside.

note.hinglish: Price per million tokens se cost nikalna ek line ka kaam hai.
note.en: Cost from per-million prices is a one-line method.

prompt.hinglish: `Call` dataclass banao (`model`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`) aur `cost()` method jo per-million prices 0.4 aur 1.6 use kare. Do calls ka total cost print karo.
prompt.en: Build a `Call` dataclass (`model`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`) with a `cost()` method using per-million prices 0.4 and 1.6. Print the total cost of two calls.

exercises.starter:
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Call:
    model: str
    prompt_tokens: int
    completion_tokens: int

    def cost(self):
        ...

calls = [Call('mini', 1000, 500), Call('mini', 2000, 1000)]
total = sum(c.cost() for c in calls)
print(round(total, 6))
exercises.solution:
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Call:
    model: str
    prompt_tokens: int
    completion_tokens: int

    def cost(self, price_in=0.4, price_out=1.6):
        return (self.prompt_tokens * price_in + self.completion_tokens * price_out) / 1_000_000

calls = [Call('mini', 1000, 500), Call('mini', 2000, 1000)]
total = sum(c.cost() for c in calls)
print(round(total, 6))

intro.hinglish: Formula yaad karne ki zaroorat nahi, intuition chahiye: vector kya hai, similarity kaise napte hain, gradient kis direction me neeche jata hai, aur probability se decision kaise nikalta hai. Loss, embeddings aur A/B tests sab isi par khade hain.
intro.en: You do not need memorised formulas, you need intuition: what a vector is, how similarity is measured, which way a gradient goes down, and how probability turns into a decision. Losses, embeddings and A/B tests all stand on this.

real_life.hinglish: Do gaano ki similarity: dono ke features (tempo, mood) ka angle jitna chhota, utne zyada similar. Cosine similarity bas wahi angle naapti hai.
real_life.en: Two songs are similar when their feature arrows point the same way. Cosine similarity measures exactly that angle.

takeaway.hinglish: Cosine direction dekhta hai, magnitude nahi; isliye text embeddings me popular hai.
takeaway.en: Cosine looks at direction, not magnitude, which is why text embeddings use it.

examples.code:
import math

def cosine(a, b):
    dot = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))
    na = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a))
    nb = math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b))
    return dot / (na * nb)

print(round(cosine([1, 0], [1, 0]), 3), round(cosine([1, 0], [0, 1]), 3))

prompt.hinglish: `cosine(a, b)` implement karo aur do pairs print karo: `[1, 2, 3]` vs `[2, 4, 6]`, aur `[1, 0]` vs `[0, 1]`.
prompt.en: Implement `cosine(a, b)` and print two pairs: `[1, 2, 3]` vs `[2, 4, 6]`, and `[1, 0]` vs `[0, 1]`.

exercises.solution:
import math

def cosine(a, b):
    dot = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))
    na = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a))
    nb = math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b))
    return dot / (na * nb)

sim = cosine([1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 6])
orthogonal = cosine([1, 0], [0, 1])
print(round(sim, 3), round(orthogonal, 3))

hint.hinglish: `[2, 4, 6]` `[1, 2, 3]` ka exact double hai, isliye angle 0 hai.
hint.en: `[2, 4, 6]` is exactly double `[1, 2, 3]`, so the angle is zero.

question.en: Cosine similarity of 0 means?

why.hinglish: 0 angle 1 deta hai, 90 degree 0; isliye 0 ka matlab koi shared direction nahi.
why.en: Zero angle gives 1, ninety degrees gives 0, so 0 means no shared direction.

question.hinglish: Gradient descent kis direction me step leta hai?
question.en: Which direction does gradient descent step?

options: Gradient ke opposite, loss kam karne ke liye
Gradient ke saath, loss badhane ke liye

why.hinglish: Gradient sabse tezi se upar jata hai; opposite jane par loss girta hai.
why.en: The gradient points uphill fastest; going opposite lowers the loss.

question.hinglish: Entropy kis cheez ko naapti hai?
question.en: What does entropy measure?

why.hinglish: Jitni uncertain distribution, utni zyada entropy; cross-entropy loss isi se aata hai.
why.en: The more uncertain the distribution, the higher the entropy; cross-entropy loss comes from it.

intro.hinglish: Zyada tar AI kaam data ka kaam hai. Groupby aur merge se sawaal ka jawab nikalta hai, cleaning se answer bharosemand hota hai, aur leakage se result jhootha 'great' lagta hai. Split pehle karo, EDA baad me.
intro.en: Most AI work is data work. Groupby and merge answer the question, cleaning makes the answer trustworthy, and leakage makes a result look falsely great. Split first, EDA after.

real_life.hinglish: Class ke marks ka average nikalna groupby hai; do sheets ko roll number par milana merge hai. Agar answer dekh kar features banao, to exam me cheating ho rahi hai — data me bhi wahi leakage hai.
real_life.en: A class average is groupby; matching two sheets on roll number is merge. Building features after seeing the answer is cheating in an exam, and the same leakage in data.

takeaway.hinglish: Har feature ke liye poochho: kya ye value prediction ke waqt really available hogi?
takeaway.en: For every feature ask: would this value really be available at prediction time?

examples.code:
from collections import defaultdict

rows = [('Pune', 200), ('Pune', 400), ('Delhi', 300)]
totals, counts = defaultdict(int), defaultdict(int)
for city, amount in rows:
    totals[city] += amount
    counts[city] += 1
print({city: totals[city] / counts[city] for city in totals})

note.hinglish: Do dictionaries se group mean nikalta hai; pandas isi ka shortcut hai.
note.en: Two dictionaries give a group mean; pandas is the shortcut for this.

examples.code:
# Plain lists - koi library nahi. Train aur test ka pattern alag hai.
train = [10.0, 12.0, 11.0]
test = [500.0, 520.0]

leaky_fill = sum(train + test) / len(train + test)   # test pehle dekh liya
honest_fill = sum(train) / len(train)                # sirf train

def mae(values, fill):
    return sum(abs(v - fill) for v in values) / len(values)

print("leaky  fill:", round(leaky_fill, 1), "| test MAE:", round(mae(test, leaky_fill), 1))
print("honest fill:", round(honest_fill, 1), "| test MAE:", round(mae(test, honest_fill), 1))
print("\nLeaky number sundar lagta hai - isliye ye khatarnak hai.")

question.en: What is data leakage?

options: Training me aisi information aana jo prediction ke waqt available nahi hogi
Data ka file se memory me load hona

why.hinglish: Leakage se test score bahut achha lagta hai, production me wahi model fail hota hai.
why.en: Leakage makes the test score look great and the production model fail.

question.hinglish: Missing values ko mean se bharne se pehle kya karna chahiye?
question.en: What should happen before filling missing values with the mean?

options: Sirf training data se mean nikaalna, test par apply karna

why.hinglish: Poore dataset ka mean test ki information training me le aata hai.
why.en: The full-dataset mean brings test information into training.

question.hinglish: Merge kis cheez par hota hai?
question.en: What does a merge join on?

why.hinglish: Join key decide karti hai kaunsi row kis row se milegi.
why.en: The join key decides which row matches which.

intro.hinglish: SQL joins, GROUP BY aur indexes roz kaam aate hain; vector database usi idea ka AI version hai — nearest neighbours dhoondhna. Postgres + pgvector aaj ka practical default hai.
intro.en: SQL joins, GROUP BY and indexes are daily tools; a vector database is the AI version of the same idea, finding nearest neighbours. Postgres + pgvector is today's practical default.

real_life.hinglish: Library me book dhoondhna: index se seedha shelf par jao, poora hall mat chhaano. ANN index bhi billions vectors me se nearest wale jaldi nikalta hai.
real_life.en: Finding a book in a library: use the index and go to the shelf instead of scanning the hall. An ANN index finds nearest vectors quickly among billions.

takeaway.hinglish: Pehle sahi schema aur index, phir fancy vector DB; 90% product SQL + ek vector column se ban jate hain.
takeaway.en: Right schema and index first, fancy vector DB later; 90% of products are SQL plus one vector column.

question.en: What does an index speed up?

why.hinglish: Index lookup O(log n) jaisa banata hai, par har write par maintain karna padta hai.
why.en: An index makes lookups roughly O(log n) but must be maintained on writes.

question.hinglish: Vector database me ANN ka matlab?
question.en: What does ANN mean in a vector database?

options: Approximate nearest neighbours — thoda approximate, bahut fast

why.hinglish: Exact search slow hota hai; ANN index speed ke liye thodi accuracy trade karta hai.
why.en: Exact search is slow; an ANN index trades a little accuracy for speed.

question.en: When do you need GROUP BY?

options: Jab har group ka aggregate (count, sum, avg) chahiye

why.hinglish: GROUP BY rows ko buckets me daalta hai, aggregate har bucket par chalta hai.
why.en: GROUP BY puts rows into buckets and aggregates each bucket.
